title: União Europeia propõe barrar menores em redes sociais, jogos online e chatbots
content: A União Europeia prepara uma proposta de lei para restringir o acesso de menores de 15 anos a redes sociais, plataformas de compartilhamento de vídeos, chatbots de inteligência artificial e jogos online. Segundo um rascunho de documento legal obtido pela AFP, o chamado EU KIDS Act impediria que crianças e adolescentes abaixo dessa idade criassem contas de forma autônoma, com regras diferentes conforme a faixa etária e maior participação dos pais. A proposta também prevê que as empresas adotem o princípio de “segurança por design”, com mudanças na forma como os serviços são desenvolvidos para reduzir riscos ao público infantil. Entre as medidas citadas estão a retirada de recursos considerados potencialmente viciantes, como rolagem infinita, notificações artificiais e determinados sistemas de recompensa. A iniciativa ganhou força após a pressão de países, como França e Grécia, e medidas adotadas pela Austrália, que proibiu o acesso de menores de 16 anos a determinadas plataformas. Na União Europeia, porém, a proposta estabelece regras diferentes de acordo com a idade do usuário. A Comissão Europeia também prevê uma taxa de supervisão cobrada das próprias plataformas para financiar a fiscalização. As novas regras devem complementar o Ato de Serviços Digitais (DSA), que já estabelece obrigações para grandes serviços digitais e prevê multas de até 6% do faturamento global anual das empresas. No entanto, o documento cita que as regras vigentes do DSA “não são suficientes” porque falta uma proibição direta e definitiva contra recursos problemáticos e viciantes. A UE ainda planeja lançar um aplicativo de verificação de idade para auxiliar no cumprimento das restrições e impedir que menores acessem serviços classificados como de risco. UE propõe limite de idade gradual A proposta europeia adota uma abordagem diferente da australiana. Enquanto a Austrália estabeleceu uma restrição geral para menores de 16 anos, o projeto da UE prevê níveis de acesso conforme a idade, com diferentes graus de participação dos responsáveis. A partir dos 15 anos, será possível criar uma conta autônoma nos serviços abrangidos pela legislação. Para adolescentes de 13 e 14 anos, o acesso dependerá da autorização dos pais para a criação de “contas introdutórias”, com recursos limitados, controle de tempo de tela e supervisão parental. Já crianças de 3 a 13 anos poderão acessar apenas contas totalmente controladas pelos pais, em serviços classificados como adequados para o público infantil. Responsabilidade das empresas de tecnologia O rascunho estabelece que as regras devem colocar a responsabilidade sobre as empresas de tecnologia, com mecanismos de proteção incorporados aos próprios serviços. Entre as medidas previstas estão: Privacidade por padrão: contas de menores devem ser privadas e as configurações consideradas de maior risco ficam desativadas; Restrição de contato: usuários desconhecidos não poderão entrar em contato com menores; Controle de algoritmos: sistemas de recomendação devem ser ajustados para reduzir a exposição de crianças a conteúdos prejudiciais; Regras específicas: chatbots de IA e jogos online terão diretrizes próprias de proteção para o público infantil. A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, deve apresentar as diretrizes gerais durante seu discurso anual ao Parlamento Europeu, em Estrasburgo. A apresentação detalhada deve ocorrer posteriormente com a participação de Henna Virkkunen, responsável pela área digital da UE. O projeto ainda não é uma lei. Depois da apresentação, a proposta terá de passar por negociações entre o Parlamento Europeu e os Estados-membros antes de entrar em vigor. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ECA Digital: o que muda para redes sociais a partir de agora”. {{WHATSAPP_CHANNEL}}

title: Menos coches y más motos en el parque móvil de la València postcovid
content:
Menos coches y más motos en el parque móvil de la València postcovid
Movilidad
La semana de la movilidad enfrenta a gobierno local y oposición en una guerra de cifras por el tráfico
Una retahíla de motocicletas, hasta 30 en una acera, yacen aparcadas en la céntrica calle Garrigues de València. En la de San Vicente hay tres aparcamientos para recarga de eléctricos, uno de ellos ocupado por una BMW, conectado en esos momentos. En las calles que bordean la plaza del Ayuntamiento se perciben casi más motocicletas que coches, en una ciudad que reordenó su tráfico en el centro hace unos años, coincidiendo con la pandemia. Desde entonces, el parque móvil de la ciudad se ha reducido un 1,8%, según los datos de la DGT en la ciudad.
De los 513.747 vehículos en 2020 se ha pasado a los 504.178: solo las motocicletas y los remolques y tractores industriales han aumentado en número. Las primeras, un 12,7%; los segundos, un 9,15%. El resto, según las cifras oficiales, han disminuido entre un 2% de los autobuses y un 24,2% de los ciclomotores. Con todo, la movilidad en la ciudad se siente menos fluida, y en ella juega un papel fundamental el área metropolitana, como bien se vio en la dana y ayer mismo: un accidente en la V-21 complicó la entrada a València a primera hora que generó tres quilómetros de retención.
Muchos trabajadores llegan en coche a la capital, como ha explicado la UPV en un reciente análisis donde asegura que desde 2022 se ha producido un incremento del tráfico en los accesos principales a la ciudad de entorno a un 5%. Clave es esta idea: prácticamente toda la población de la ciudad tiene algún servicio de movilidad a menos de cinco minutos a pie de su vivienda, pero esta desciende hasta el 46% al analizar el área metropolitana.
Sus residentes usan Cercanías o Metrovalencia, cuyos tornos permanecían ayer abiertos por el Día sin Coches. Tampoco gastaba viajes del bonobús quien viajaba con la EMT, aunque muchos ni se dieran cuenta de que la máquina advertía del “viaje gratis”. “He pasado la tarjeta, ni lo sabía”, decía una señora con el Bono Oro en la mano. Los más avispados se llevaron uno de los 500 bonobuses que el Ayuntamiento escondió en distintos autobuses y, confirmó después, que habían sido encontrados, todos, a primera hora. Los podrán usar hoy, ayer se insistía en que el día era de viaje gratuito para fomentar un transporte público muy cuestionado en los últimos años.
Compromís alega que la media diaria de vehículos se ha incrementado un 146,6% en la calle Colón desde que gobierna Catalá
Algunos conductores sabían de la sorpresa “porque lo he leído en redes sociales”, otros pasaban la mañana como siempre, evitando cargas y descargas atestadas, dobles filas -tan típicas de València- y recogiendo a viajeros. En aspecto, la de ayer fue una jornada más para el tráfico en la capital, sobre todo en su centro, que sigue obstruido por las obras de la calle Colón y cuánto esto supone para las vías aledañas.
Es uno de los motivos de enfrentamiento entre gobierno local y oposición, que afea con datos el aumento del tráfico rodado. Compromís alega que la media diaria de vehículos se ha incrementado un 146,6% en la calle Colón desde que gobiernan PP y Vox, además de señalar un aumento de quejas de usuarios de la EMT, que sitúan en un 15,9% en junio de 2026 más que en 2025 y un 7,1% en el acumulado del año, mientras que “ha cerrado 2025 con récord de viajeros y la misma flota que en 2024”. A esto, el concejal de movilidad, Jesús Carbonell, contesta que hay en marcha un plan de inversiones de 172 millones que incluye la compra de 222 autobuses y la contratación de 160 conductores; y sobre los accesos de la calle Colón, que los vehículos que ahora pasan por ahí son “los que dejan de pasar por la Gran Vía”.

title: Serum Na-Cl value from routine blood tests reflects CO<sub>2</sub> retention in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
content: by Isamu Yamakawa, Ryota Tamura, Hiroyuki Yabata, Takahito Tsukamoto, Shuhei Kobashi, Yoshitaka Tamaki, Nobuhiro Ogawa, Akihiro Kitamura, Makoto Urushitani Background Respiratory failure is the leading cause of death in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Early detection of CO2 retention is crucial for assessing respiratory failure severity and guiding noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (NPPV) management. However, arterial blood gas analysis is invasive and uncomfortable for routine monitoring. Objective We investigated whether the serum sodium-chloride difference (Na-Cl value), calculated from routine blood tests, could serve as a screening marker for CO2 retention in ALS patients. Methods This retrospective study included 88 ALS patients with 116 paired samples of arterial blood gas and serum electrolyte data. We analyzed correlations between Na-Cl value and blood gas parameters (HCO3−, PCO2), performed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis for detecting CO2 retention (PCO2 ≥ 45 mmHg), and examined relationships with respiratory function (%FVC). Results Na-Cl value showed strong correlation with HCO3− (r = 0.78, p < 0.001) and PCO2 (r = 0.71, p < 0.001). Na-Cl ≥ 37 mEq/L demonstrated sensitivity of 85.11% and specificity of 69.57% for detecting PCO2 ≥ 45 mmHg, with negative predictive value of 87.27% (AUC = 0.842). Na-Cl ≥ 39 mEq/L achieved specificity of 92.75%. Patients with %FVC < 50% had significantly higher Na-Cl, PCO2, and HCO3− values. Conclusions Serum Na-Cl value serves as a simple, noninvasive screening marker for CO2 retention in ALS. Na-Cl ≥ 37 mEq/L warrants blood gas analysis, while Na-Cl ≥ 39 mEq/L provides specificity >90%. This marker can be calculated from routine blood tests without additional cost, making it suitable for frequent monitoring and reducing the risk of missing intervention timing.

title: Biogas Fertilizer Boosts Soil Microbes and Apple Quality on the Loess Plateau
content:
On the dusty, wind-scoured terraces of China’s semiarid Loess Plateau, apple growers have long wrestled with a stubborn paradox: the region’s deep, well-drained loess soils are ideal for fruit trees, yet decades of intensive cultivation and heavy chemical fertilization have left many orchards degraded, compacted, and starved of organic matter. Now, a three-year field experiment conducted by researchers at Gansu Agricultural University suggests that a humble byproduct of rural waste management—biogas fertilizer, the nutrient-rich slurry left over after anaerobic digestion—may offer a way to rebuild these tired soils from the ground up, with measurable benefits that ripple upward through soil microbes, tree physiology, and ultimately the apples themselves.
The study, published in BMC Plant Biology, was led by Baozhen Zeng, Yongjuan Cheng, and colleagues from the College of Horticulture at Gansu Agricultural University in Lanzhou, with Juan Mao serving as corresponding author. The team set out to answer a deceptively simple question: how do different fertilization schemes, particularly those incorporating biogas fertilizer, shape the physical and chemical properties of orchard soil, the structure and function of its microbial communities, the physiological performance of apple trees, and the quality of the fruit they bear? Because the Loess Plateau is one of China’s most important apple-producing regions, the answer carries weight far beyond a handful of experimental plots.
The researchers ran their field experiment over three growing seasons, comparing several fertilization regimes that differed in whether and how much biogas fertilizer was applied. The apple variety under study was ‘Yanfu 3’, a cultivar widely grown in the region. The team then tracked an unusually comprehensive suite of variables: soil water-holding capacity, soil organic matter, nutrient availability, cation exchange capacity, and pH; the composition and diversity of the soil microbial community; leaf nutrient accumulation and photosynthetic performance; and, finally, fruit size, colouration, sugar composition, and bioactive compounds. Supplementary analyses included rarefaction and rank-abundance curves, principal component analysis, non-metric multidimensional scaling with PERMANOVA testing, and detailed vertical profiles of macro- and micronutrients—nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, iron, manganese, zinc, and copper—across soil layers and years.
The headline finding is that fertilization regimes incorporating biogas fertilizer were consistently associated with better soil conditions. Soils receiving biogas showed increased water-holding capacity—a critical trait in a semiarid region where every millimetre of stored moisture counts—alongside higher soil organic matter content, greater nutrient availability, and improved cation exchange capacity, the soil’s ability to hold onto positively charged nutrients such as potassium, ammonium, calcium, and magnesium. Perhaps just as importantly, biogas-amended soils maintained a pH within the range of roughly 6.5 to 7.5, the window in which most nutrients remain maximally available to tree roots. In acidified or alkalized soils, nutrients can become chemically locked away even when total reserves are ample; keeping pH in the neutral band is one of the quiet achievements of good organic management.
Depth mattered. The beneficial effects of biogas incorporation were most pronounced in the top 0 to 20 centimetres of soil, the layer where apple trees concentrate much of their fine-root activity and where most microbial biomass resides. The effects also became more evident as application rates increased, pointing to a dose-responsive relationship rather than a simple yes-or-no effect. For growers, this suggests that the surface layer—often the most vulnerable to erosion, drying, and nutrient depletion—is precisely where organic amendments deliver their greatest returns.
Beneath the visible improvements in soil chemistry, the study documented a parallel transformation in the soil’s living community. Biogas-fertilized plots showed shifts in microbial community composition and diversity, with a notable enrichment of functional groups involved in organic matter decomposition and nutrient cycling. In practical terms, this means the soil microbiome was recalibrated toward organisms that break down complex organic residues and convert them into plant-available forms of nitrogen, phosphorus, and other nutrients. Such communities act as the digestive system of the orchard: when they are abundant and active, organic inputs are efficiently mineralized, and nutrients circulate rather than accumulate in inaccessible forms. The multivariate statistical analyses confirmed that samples from different treatments clustered distinctly, indicating that fertilization regime left a detectable fingerprint on the entire microbial assemblage.
Those below-ground changes translated into above-ground gains. Trees growing in biogas-amended soils accumulated more nutrients in their leaves and showed enhanced photosynthetic performance, the engine that converts sunlight into the sugars and carbon skeletons that build fruit. Leaf nutrient status is a well-established diagnostic of tree health in horticulture, and improved photosynthesis provides the raw material for everything a grower ultimately sells. The chain of causation proposed by the authors runs cleanly from soil to microbe to leaf to fruit: better soil structure and fertility support a more functional microbiome, which supplies nutrients more effectively, which powers the canopy, which feeds the crop.
And the crop responded. Fruit from trees under biogas-inclusive regimes showed improvements in size, colouration, sugar composition, and bioactive compounds—the suite of traits that determine whether an apple commands a premium price at market. Colouration reflects anthocyanin accumulation and light interception within the canopy; sugar composition governs sweetness and flavour balance; and bioactive compounds contribute to nutritional value and storage quality. Among all the regimes tested, the treatment delivering 90 kilograms of biogas fertilizer per tree produced the most favourable overall performance under the experimental conditions, offering growers a concrete starting point for calibrating their own application rates.
The authors are careful to frame their conclusions with appropriate scientific caution. Because the different treatments involved different total nutrient inputs, the observed effects reflect integrated fertilization outcomes rather than the isolated effect of biogas fertilizer itself. In other words, some of the benefit may stem simply from supplying more nutrients in a more balanced form, rather than from any unique property of the biogas slurry. This distinction matters for interpretation, but it does not diminish the practical message: schemes that integrate biogas fertilizer, as applied in this study, outperformed the alternatives across soil, microbial, physiological, and fruit-quality metrics simultaneously.
The broader implications extend into sustainability and circular agriculture. Biogas fertilizer is a product of anaerobic digestion of organic wastes such as manure and crop residues, so integrating it into orchard management closes a nutrient loop: farm waste becomes fuel, and the digested residue returns to the soil as fertilizer. In a semiarid region where soil degradation and low nutrient use efficiency have constrained sustainable productivity, this dual benefit—waste recycling and soil restoration—is especially attractive. The study’s authors position their findings as a basis for optimizing organic fertilization strategies in semiarid apple orchards, and with three years of field data spanning soil physics, microbiology, tree physiology, and fruit chemistry, they have built one of the more complete evidence chains linking what farmers put into the ground with what consumers eventually bite into. For the apple growers of the Loess Plateau, the path to sweeter, redder, larger fruit may run straight through the digester.

title: Video captures ranger's joyful tears on finding rare night parrot chick
content:
Rare video of night parrot chick hiding in spinifex tunnel in WA desert
In short:
A young night parrot, one of Australia's most cryptic birds, has been filmed in a spinifex tunnel in remote WA.
The daytime footage captures the elation of a ranger team as they make the rare discovery of the bird in the grassy nest.
What's next?
Rangers for the Ngururrpa Indigenous Protected Area are working with scientists to develop an eDNA program for finding signs of night parrots in waterholes.
Even in the heart of night parrot country it can be rare to actually see one of the world's most cryptic birds.
That is why the discovery of a young night parrot (Pezoporus occidentalis) this year set off an outpouring of emotion in the middle of the Great Sandy Desert in Western Australia.
A new video captures the moment members of the Ngururrpa Rangers and researchers shout-whisper through joyful tears on finding a nestling.
The sighting was even more unique because it happened during daytime, when critically endangered night parrots, as their name suggests, were hidden away.
Night parrots were thought extinct until they were rediscovered in 2013 in Queensland.
While the Ngururrpa Indigenous Protected Area is home to one of the largest populations of the species, this is the first time some rangers have seen a live bird in the area.
Kathryn Njamme, a member of the Ngururrpa Rangers, had previously heard the chime-like call of the bird. She had even seen camera trap footage, an egg and their loose green and yellow feathers.
But she had not laid eyes directly on a living night parrot.
"We was really happy and excited to find a night parrot," Ms Njamme said.
"We all was crying there and holding each other.
"We wanted to show people around the world that there's a night parrot out there in the country."
How the parrot was found
Ms Njamme said during a July trip to the Ngururrpa Indigenous Protected Area she sought help at a spirit tree.
"That's where we asked the Old People to help us find these birds," she said.
"We asked the Old People if they can reveal it for us so we can find them out in the bush when we drew the rain."
A few nights into the trip, there was heavy rain over the desert.
The next morning the rangers went searching among the old-growth mounds of bull spinifex (Triodia longiceps), called "lanu lanu" in Kukatja language, which night parrots are known to use as nests and shelter.
Ms Njamme said that was when ranger Lucinda Gibson found a wet feather in the spinifex.
"She went round to look at that [feather] and she found that burrow [in the grass]," she said.
"That spinifex is a bit grey but she saw little bit of colours on it like yellow and green.
"That's when she noticed that night parrot was in the burrow."
Ms Gibson whistled and gave a hand signal of a flapping bird to Ms Njamme and the rest of the searchers.
Adult night parrots typically sport a coat of green and yellow feathers with black highlights.
But the rangers could see the juvenile bird still had a lot of grey and soft wispy feathers, which helped it blend into the grey interior of the spinifex lump.
Ms Njamme said the parrot may have been perched high in the spinifex because of the damp ground from the rain.
"It was a bit wet on the bottom, that's why he had to move up."
Ngururrpa Indigenous Protected Area coordinator Christy Davies said the parrot was quiet and looked like it was close to the fledgling stage, when a bird learns to fly.
"A lot of young birds and baby birds … unless they're being fed by the parents, they just sit still and don't make a sound," she said.
"So that's what it was doing, just sitting there, not making a sound and relying on its camouflage to protect it."
Turbocharging the search for night parrots
While the moment of finding a juvenile night parrot may seem fortuitous, there is also deep knowledge behind knowing where to look.
By combining what is known about night parrot preferences with cultural knowledge, Ngururrpa Rangers have built a model for finding likely habitat in their region.
The habitat model was developed in a research partnership with the National Environmental Science Program and the Indigenous Desert Alliance.
"A lot of [rangers] have identified areas of likely habitat because they know where that lanu lanu is," Ms Davies said.
"They know where the water sources are and the seasonality of those water sources and where different plants are that form a component of the [parrot] feeding habitats.
"So it's understanding where those different components are that the night parrots need that helps us hone in on particular areas."
Knowing more about where the parrot lives and how many there are will help with conservation efforts to make sure it does not go extinct from threats like feral cats and unmanaged fire.
Rangers are also hoping to use and develop new tools to find the hidden parrots.
An AI tool is being developed to analyse thousands of hours of desert recordings to find likely night parrot calls.
And an environmental DNA (eDNA)analysis technique is in the fine-tuning stage for helping detect if a night parrot has recently used a water source.
Ms Njamme said the eDNA tool could potentially be used by other groups around the country to find and help night parrots.
"We don't see much night parrot, [but] we're trying to look after them."

title: Implementation of global agreements needs deeper integration – the UNCCD COP17 provides a pathway
content:
The latest UN climate summit in Mongolia highlighted a familiar tension. While agreements were forged on land and agriculture, crucial action on drought was repeatedly deferred. This pattern raises urgent questions about the efficacy of consensus-driven negotiation.
Beyond the formal talks, however, a different story unfolded. Coalitions formed, investment was unlocked, and diverse voices were heard, pointing towards a more integrated pathway for tackling interconnected crises. The challenge now is to translate this broader engagement into tangible, scaled solutions.

Broad cooperation between national governments, international organisations, civil society and the private sector delivered long-needed prioritisation of rangelands and grasslands, and food and agricultural systems transformation. However, the need for consensus meant progress in other key areas, for instance on how to tackle drought, was limited by national or regional disagreements.
So how can future summits build on what worked, scale solutions, and harness the momentum for accelerated action on nature, climate and food security crises?
Is consensus enough to accelerate implementation?
The three Rio Convention COPs were initially conceptualised as political negotiating spaces, where countries would agree on how to address multiple environmental crises such as climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation and desertification.
Significant progress has been made under this model of international consensus, including securing breakthrough agreements on climate and biodiversity. However, the model has come increasingly under strain, including at the recent 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD).
Parties could not agree on much-needed action on drought resilience and preparedness, opting to defer a decision to COP18 in 2028, despite doing the same thing at COP16 in 2024. Ambition on several other issues was limited due to Parties adopting hard lines. Critics have used such stumbling blocks as indications that the COP model, based on achieving consensus, is no longer fit for purpose.
Nonetheless, formal negotiations across multilateral forums remain important, and can still deliver important progress. And in Mongolia, negotiated decisions were agreed on previously overlooked solutions to the joint nature, climate and food security agenda: to protect, sustainably manage and restore once-ignored rangelands and grasslands; support underserved pastoralists and local communities; and transition to nature-positive agriculture.
Increasing opportunity through integrated approaches
Yet what happens in formal negotiations is just one way in which the success of UNCCD COP17, and indeed other COPs, should be judged. COPs have evolved beyond formal negotiations. They now reflect the reality that, alongside international policy, systemic transformation requires collaboration across coalitions of countries, the unlocking of investment, wider public sector and private sector action, and the direct involvement of Indigenous Peoples, local communities, youth and women in decision-making processes.
This point was continuously reinforced by UNCCD Executive Secretary Yasmine Fouad, and the energy on the ground reflected this wider picture. Of course, there were frustrations at deadlocks in negotiations, but there was also optimism and determination to advance solutions and scale impact through all available mechanisms.
For example, the Rangelands Flagship Initiative was launched to build a pipeline of programmes, with $1.2 bn of funding already mobilised, the largest rangelands and grasslands investment commitment in UNCCD history.
A $400m Drought Resilience Investment Facility was also launched alongside a new tool to support countries in anticipating, preparing for and adapting to drought. A landmark declaration providing greater recognition of pastoralists as environmental stewards, with stronger participation in decision-making and direct access to finance and support, was adopted.
And the COP31 Presidency Process, led by Türkiye, was launched to support country-led integration of existing national actions across climate, biodiversity and land.
Scaling solutions that work
This is the energy and drive that must be carried into biological diversity (CBD) COP17 in Yerevan, climate change (UNFCCC) COP31 in Antalya, and beyond. Ambition should not be tempered; impact can be created through multistakeholder action and deepening synergies between land, nature and climate plans.
Take the work in Mongolia to restore degraded grasslands in the Eastern Steppe as an example. Overgrazing from increased livestock populations in concentrated areas, combined with climate change, has been eroding soil health, putting local livelihoods and biodiversity at risk.
But a five-year project implemented by WWF, FAO and the Mongolian Ministry of Environment and Climate Change has used a landscape plan that includes rotational grazing and nature-positive agricultural practices to restore the landscape.
Local herders have informed regional planning. More than 835,000 hectares have been improved, more than 15 million hectares are now covered in new legal frameworks for sustainable pasture management, and over 19 million tons of carbon dioxide (CO2) have been sequestered through sustainable land management practices, with continued benefits expected.
A problem that arose from connected issues has been addressed with an integrated solution, anchored around food and agricultural transformation. These are the types of solutions that need to be celebrated, financed and scaled. COPs present a crucial opportunity to elevate actions that we already know work, to accelerate collaboration and deepen synergies.
UNCCD COP17 laid solid foundations for increased impact. By bringing food and agriculture and grasslands to the front and centre of the land and water management agenda, it created new hope for billions of people. But hope alone doesn’t put food on the table, limit global warming or restore nature.
The biodiversity COP (CBD COP17) and UNFCCC COP31 must build on these foundations to increase the funding pipeline for integrated projects that can be rapidly deployed – delivering real benefits to people and nature.
João Campari is the global food and agriculture leader at WWF

title: Ecuador lodge pays farmers for bear damage, helping spectacled bears live wild
content:
An Ecuador wildlife lodge is pairing bear watching with a compensation program for nearby farmers, giving visitors a rare look at wild spectacled bears while reducing pressure on local people to push the animals away.
By linking tourism to reimbursement for crop losses, the lodge uses revenue to support both conservation and the communities living closest to the bears.
Here's what to know
Zach O'Neill, a conservation educator, spotlighted Ecuador's Bear Canyon Lodge in an Instagram post, focusing on how the property works to protect spectacled bears.
As O'Neill explained, when spectacled bears raid nearby farms or cause other damage to agricultural areas, the lodge reimburses farmers instead of leaving them to cover the losses themselves.
As the only bear species in South America, spectacled bears can run into trouble when they feed near agricultural lands.
As O'Neill's caption explained, "Farmers may try to scare or even eliminate spectacled bears due to damages to their crops," but the lodge's payments help the animals "live safely and free from persecution for simply following their natural instincts."
What's being done?
When bears harm crops or other property, Bear Canyon Lodge provides farmers with direct compensation. By lowering the chance of retaliation, that support improves the bears' odds of continuing to live in the wild.
O'Neill added in the caption: "Their approach to wildlife observation is not only ethical and respectful to the animals, but also helps to ensure their future as a species."
In the words of Danilo Vasquez, who founded the lodge and has worked there for over two decades, this is "a project of coexistence."
Where can I learn more?
Bear conservation often comes down to what happens at the edge of farms, ranches, and tourist destinations. These articles look at the same balancing act Bear Canyon Lodge is navigating, helping people and bears share space safely.
• On working farms, ranchers are using incredible guardians to protect livestock without killing bears.
• In Montana, the Interior Department is funding efforts to prevent grizzly bear encounters near ranches.
• In Spain, local officials formed a protective bear task force after human encounters increased.
Coexistence with wildlife works best when local communities have practical tools and real support. Bear Canyon Lodge's compensation model fits squarely within that broader conservation playbook.

title: Deadline Nears For Education Department To Spend Special Ed Research Funds
content:
Deadline Nears For Education Department To Spend Special Ed Research Funds
For months, there have been concerns that the U.S. Department of Education could allow millions in special education research dollars to lapse. Now, a federal judge is stepping in.
U.S. District Judge Allison D. Burroughs is ordering the Education Department to update her by Monday about the status of the government’s education research funds.
As of last week, about $180 million in funding for the Education Department’s Institute of Education Sciences, or IES, which handles statistics, research and evaluation, remained unallocated and is set to expire at the end of September, Burroughs said. It’s unclear how much of that is intended for special education.
Advertisement - Continue Reading Below
The situation comes after a report this spring warned that just $11 million out of $77 million in the government’s budget for special education research and evaluation program had been spoken for. Subsequently, the National Center for Learning Disabilities, the Massachusetts Teachers Association and other stakeholders sued to prevent the funds from lapsing.
Burroughs said she opted to take a soft touch in the case based on assurances from the Education Department “that they intend to obligate the funds at issue before the deadline.”
However, she noted that “if it appears, as September 30 approaches, that defendants have misled the court and the funds will not be obligated by the deadline, the court may reconsider whether there has been undue delay warranting injunctive relief.”
Despite the agency’s assurances to the court, however, the status of the funding remains murky.
Meghan Burke, a professor of special education at Vanderbilt University, said that so far this year there have only been five awards from the National Center for Special Education Research, the special education funding arm of IES. All of the grants began this month. That volume is “lower than a typical year,” she said.
Jacqueline Rodriguez, CEO of the National Center for Learning Disabilities, which is part of the litigation, said she believes that it’s realistic for the funds to be released in light of the government’s assurances, but has limited information to go on.
“We don’t have a current number for exactly how much special education research funding remains unspent because the government has not publicly updated those figures,” Rodriguez said. But, she noted that requests for proposals have gone out, which she said was likely spurred by the lawsuit.
Preventing the funding from expiring, however, is critical, Rodriguez said.
“This funding supports research that gives us a much clearer picture of what students with disabilities are experiencing in schools and where they are not getting the support they need. It also supports work that benefits students in general education, as well as technical assistance that helps families understand and participate in the special education process,” she said. “If we don’t have that research and support, we’re making decisions without the information we need to know whether we’re actually serving students well.”
The Department of Education did not respond to questions about how much special education research funding remains unallocated.
“IES intends to use its remaining FY25 funds to fully fund existing research grants, as well as to support other high-quality statistical and evaluation activities in service of its statutory obligations,” a department spokesperson said.
The order related to education research funds comes as a different federal judge ruled in a separate case brought by a coalition of states that the Education Department erred in the way in which it canceled hundreds of millions of dollars in grants for teacher training. The grants included funding to prepare educators to work with students with disabilities.
“The ruling is a victory for students, teachers and schools and common sense as our nation’s schools struggle with teacher training, hiring and retention,” said Stephanie Smith Lee, co-director of policy and advocacy at the National Down Syndrome Congress. She previously served as director of the Education Department’s Office of Special Education Programs under President George W. Bush.
Yet another case brought by states related to Individuals with Disabilities Education Act grants for special education teacher training has yet to be decided.

title: Povestea uimitoare a „țestoaselor extraterestre”: cum au revenit pe insula din Galapagos, de unde dispăruseră timp de două secole
content:
Povestea uimitoare a „țestoaselor extraterestre”: cum au revenit pe insula din Galapagos, de unde dispăruseră timp de două secole
Țestoasele gigantice sunt o curiozitate astăzi, trăind în sălbăticie doar în Insulele Galapagos sau în Atolul Aldabra din Oceanul Indian.
Povestea țestoaselor gigantice din Galapagos nu poate fi disociată de pirați. Începând cu secolul al XVI-lea, acești marinari au început să sosească pe insule, urmați mai târziu de vânătorii de balene, pecetluind împreună destinul sutelor de mii de exemplare care locuiau în arhipelag.
Rezistența țestoaselor gigantice, care, potrivit experților, au ajuns în Galapagos din America de Sud acum 2-3 milioane de ani, a devenit cel mai mare dezavantaj al lor: întrucât puteau supraviețui până la un an fără hrană sau apă, erau capturate de marinari, știind că vor rezista în calele navelor lor. „Și când acești oameni voiau să mănânce, țestoasele erau pur și simplu acolo și aveau carne proaspătă”, a declarat pentru CNN Jorge Carrión, directorul unei organizații care lucrează pentru conservarea arhipelagului din 1985, potrivit CNN.
În doar două secole, între 100.000 și 200.000 de broaște țestoase au dispărut de pe acele insule aproape mitice pe care Charles Darwin le-a vizitat în 1835 la bordul HMS Beagle, într-o călătorie care avea să devină esențială pentru teoria sa despre evoluție.
Țestoasele gigantice din Galapagos nu reprezintă o singură specie; fiecare insulă are propria specie de broască țestoasă care, în timp, s-a adaptat la mediul său. Mai multe dintre acestea au dispărut complet deoarece vânătorii de balene care se opreau în arhipelag le-au prins pentru hrană și au introdus alte amenințări, cum ar fi speciile invazive.
Prima care a dispărut, în jurul anului 1850, a fost broasca țestoasă Floreana, numită după insula pe care trăia. „Erau broaște țestoase foarte neobișnuite, cu o formă foarte pronunțată - ceea ce numim formă de «șa» - care nu se găsește nicăieri altundeva pe planetă”, a declarat James Gibbs, vicepreședinte pentru Știință și Conservare la Galapagos Conservancy și profesor la Universitatea de Stat din New York.
Descoperirea unor „broaște țestoase extraterestre” pe un vulcan îndepărtat
În timpul unei expediții din anul 2000 la vulcanul Wolf, cel mai înalt punct din Insulele Galapagos, situat în vârful nordic al insulei Isabela, cercetătorii conduși de Gibbs au descoperit broaște țestoase cu o formă de carapace neobișnuită pentru zonă.
„Erau mii de specii native acolo... dar a devenit repede clar că existau și niște broaște țestoase ciudate”, își amintește Gibbs, a cărui legătură cu Insulele Galapagos datează de zeci de ani: a sosit ca voluntar când era doar student la universitate, iar insulele, spune el, l-au transformat, determinându-l să-și dedice viața conservării lor.
În expedițiile ulterioare, au întâlnit din nou multe dintre aceste broaște țestoase „foarte sculptate, în formă de șa”, trăind împreună în canioane înguste. „Le-am numit extratereștri pentru că nu știam ce sunt”, își amintește el. Au prelevat probe de sânge și le-au trimis geneticienilor de la Universitatea Yale, care au confirmat că existau diferențe în comparație cu speciile cunoscute de pe acea insulă și au folosit același termen: extratereștri. Patru ani mai târziu, studii genetice suplimentare au confirmat că proveneau din linia Floreana.
Dar cum a fost posibil ca acestea să fi dispărut pe o insulă și să fi reapărut 150 de ani mai târziu pe un vulcan la celălalt capăt al arhipelagului? Există două ipoteze, a spus Carrión. Una este un proces natural: atunci când sunt ploi abundente, viiturile fulgerătoare mătură tot ce le stă în cale, ceea ce ar fi putut transporta broaștele țestoase între insule. Însă oamenii de știință cred că oamenii au fost cel mai probabil responsabili.
„Rețineți că pirații și vânătorii de balene obișnuiau să vină în Galapagos și să ia zeci sau sute de broaște țestoase pe navele lor. O posibilitate este să se fi produs un accident lângă vulcanul Wolf”, explică el. Cealaltă este pur logistică: insula Isabela, datorită locației sale, era ultimul punct de control pentru nave înainte de a se aventura în Pacific. Acolo, verificau greutatea broaștelor țestoase și, dacă nava depășea limita de greutate, aruncau unele, care, din fericire pentru viitor, ar fi putut ajunge pe o insulă neașteptată.
De la incubarea ouălor până la eliberare
Centrul de creștere a țestoaselor terestre Fausto Llerena lucrează din 1965 pentru a proteja aceste reptile gigantice. Aceștia au reprodus, crescut și eliberat deja cu succes specii de pe insulele Española și Santa Fe, printre altele. Nouăsprezece exemplare din linia Floreana au fost transferate acolo după descoperirea lor pe vulcanul Wolf, pentru îngrijire și reproducere.
Freddy Villalba, de la Direcția Parcului Național Galapagos, este ranger de 23 de ani și administrează acest centru de reproducere.
Lucrează cu broaște țestoase adulte și cu ouă depuse în captivitate, cum este cazul celor de la Floreana, sau colectate din sălbăticie. Marchează, cântăresc și plasează ouăle în incubatoare la temperaturi diferite. În această etapă, sexul broaștelor țestoase este încă nedeterminat: va fi determinat de temperatura la care se dezvoltă ouăle, a spus Villalba. În incubatoarele programate la 29,5°C, se vor dezvolta broaște țestoase femele, iar în cele la 28°C, vor fi masculi.
După patru luni de incubație, ouăle eclozează, iar personalul transferă țestoasele nou-născute în cutii întunecate, cu umiditate controlată, unde vor rămâne timp de o lună, hrănindu-se exclusiv cu sacul vitelin, replicând procesul pe care l-ar trece în sălbăticie.
Treizeci de zile mai târziu, ies în incintele unde se hrănesc cu frunze tocate numite „urechi de elefant”, hrana lor pentru primii doi ani. În această etapă inițială, trebuie să fie „foarte atent protejați”, a spus Villalba, deoarece măsoară între 8 și 9 centimetri și sunt o pradă ușoară pentru prădători.
Majoritatea ţestoaselor eclozate pe plajele din Florida sunt femele, în contextul verilor mai călduroaseTehnologia NASA și urmărirea prin satelit
În februarie 2026, 158 de pui de broască țestoasă au fost eliberați pe Insula Floreana cu dispozitive de urmărire prin satelit, astfel încât oamenii de știință să poată studia cum reacționează acestea la habitatul lor și cum reacționează habitatul la ele. Cu resurse de la NASA, specialiștii au identificat cele mai bune zone pentru eliberarea lor, unde ar putea ulterior să cuibărească.
Acestea sunt descendenți ai broaștelor țestoase găsite acum mai bine de 20 de ani pe vulcan, care „au prosperat enorm”, a spus Gibbs. „Nu știi niciodată cum se vor adapta animalele aduse din sălbăticie la captivitate, dar acestea au prosperat remarcabil. Sunt mâncătoare vorace și foarte reproductive; într-un timp foarte scurt, au produs 800 de pui de broască țestoasă și vor continua să producă o medie de 60 pe an”, a adăugat Gibbs.
Walter Chimborazo, asistent de teren la Centrul de Creștere al Galapagos Conservancy, a fost martor la nașterea țestoaselor care acum cutreieră insula Floreana. „Erau atât de mici, mai mici decât palma mea”, își amintește el.
Eliberarea lor îl face fericit, desigur, dar îl lasă și cu sentimentul dulce-amar al rămas-bun. „Am petrecut mai mult timp aici la serviciu decât acasă... Pe de o parte, sunt fericit, dar pe de altă parte, sunt trist pentru că nu-i voi mai vedea cu adevărat.”
Tatăl său a lucrat la același centru de creștere a animalelor. Chimborazo știe că slujba lui este un privilegiu și este mândru că a dat totul: „Știu că am avut grijă de ei; i-am crescut. I-am învățat ca să poată supraviețui pe insula lor.”
Țestoasele eliberate recent sunt hibride, a explicat Cristian Sevilla, directorul departamentului de Ecosisteme din cadrul Parcului Național Galapagos. Structura lor genetică este parțial cea a țestoaselor Floreana, care au dispărut în secolul al XIX-lea, și parțial cea a speciilor native din zona vulcanului Wolf.
„Nu am găsit încă o broască țestoasă Floreana pură, dar credem că există. Am găsit câteva exemplare tinere pe Vulcanul Wolf, care sunt 50% Floreana și 50% specie nativă, ceea ce implică faptul că au avut în mod necesar un părinte de rasă pură”, a explicat Gibbs. „Prin urmare, este probabil ca unele să mai cutreiere întinderea acestui vulcan; poate că sunt unele dintre broaștele țestoase originale pe care vânătorii de balene le-au adus și le-au lăsat acolo.” Broaștele țestoase Floreana pot trăi mai mult de 100 de ani în sălbăticie.
Ingineri de ecosistem
Carrión a descris țestoasele gigantice drept „ingineri ecosistemici” ai arhipelagului. „Ele ajută la dispersarea semințelor. Ele ajută la construirea și modificarea comunităților de plante din ecosistemele Galapagos și, prin urmare, sunt esențiale nu doar pentru ele însele ca țestoase, ci și pentru dinamica ecologică a ecosistemelor”, a explicat el.
Cheia constă în dieta lor: fiecare broască țestoasă gigantică mănâncă până la 225 de kilograme (496 de livre) de vegetație pe an. „Procesul de digestie a unei singure îmbucături de material vegetal durează aproximativ o lună”, a spus Gibbs, „așa că rămășițele nu sunt expulzate decât după acel timp.” „Până atunci, animalul a migrat deja și a călătorit mulți kilometri, dispersând astfel cantități enorme de semințe. Și multe plante, de fapt, nu germinează foarte bine decât dacă au trecut prin tractul digestiv al unei broaște țestoase gigantice.”
Sute de ţestoase, salvate din mâinile „Bandei Ţestoaselor Ninja", în Malaysia. Unde urmau să ajungăDar, cântărind până la 400 de kilograme, sunt ca niște excavatoare, a explicat Gibbs: „Sapă prin vegetație; o aplatizează și își pregătesc paturile pentru noapte.”
„Dacă dispersează semințe, ajută alte specii să se hrănească cu aceste plante. Dacă creează spații, aceste spații sunt ocupate de alte specii, cum ar fi păsările terestre, de exemplu”, a spus Sevilla.
Prin eforturile de recuperare a țestoaselor gigantice, conservatorii restaurează acest ecosistem unic. Eforturile de conservare au eradicat, de asemenea, unele dintre speciile invazive care au ajuns odată cu oamenii, cum ar fi caprele, porcii și măgarii, și lucrează la controlul altor două amenințări majore: rozătoarele și pisicile.
Lecția țestoaselor
Țestoasele gigantice sunt o curiozitate astăzi, trăind în sălbăticie doar în Insulele Galapagos sau în Atolul Aldabra din Oceanul Indian. Au fost primele specii de megafaună care s-au răspândit în Asia, America de Sud și America de Nord. Până acum doar 10.000 de ani, locuiau chiar și în zone îndepărtate precum Florida.
Insulele Galapagos au fost locul unor activități extraordinare de conservare, un efort de colaborare între guvern, organizații civile și populația locală. Această activitate a permis creșterea în captivitate a peste 9.000 de broaște țestoase gigantice și eliberarea lor în sălbăticie în ultimii 60 de ani.
Însă recuperarea completă necesită timp. Lecția broaștelor țestoase este una a răbdării. „Cresc încet, da, dar sunt foarte constante și persistente. Este ca în fabula despre broasca țestoasă și iepure: în cele din urmă, broasca țestoasă câștigă cursa”, a reflectat Gibbs.
Și, în același timp, sunt extraordinar de nobili. După cum a spus Gibbs, „Sunt creaturi atât de rezistente, longevive și tenace încât, de fapt, ne-au permis să rezolvăm unele dintre problemele pe care le-am creat.”

title: Distinguen a guardaparques de reservas Tambopata y Asháninka por protección de la Amazonía
content:
La defensa de los bosques frente a la minería ilegal, la investigación junto a comunidades indígenas y una vida dedicada a proteger la Amazonía fueron reconocidas en el premio para la conservación Carlos Ponce del Prado 2026. Entre los galardonados figuran dos guardaparques del Servicio Nacional de Áreas Naturales Protegidas por el Estado (Sernanp) y el jefe del parque nacional Yaguas.


Abner Guevara Papa, guardaparque de la
reserva nacional Tambopata desde 2005, recibió la distinción Guardaparque ilustre. Ha participado en patrullajes, vigilancia y acciones frente a la minería y tala ilegal. Su conocimiento del área forma parte de su legado y comparte esa experiencia con nuevos guardaparques, a quienes capacita en vigilancia y en el uso de drones para detectar actividades que afectan la reserva.
“Conozco a Abner desde mi etapa como jefe de la reserva nacional Tambopata. Sé lo que significa su trabajo diario. He visto el esfuerzo que exige proteger la reserva, salir al campo día tras día, enfrentar la minería ilegal y volver a hacerlo al día siguiente", sostuvo el presidente ejecutivo del Sernanp, José Carlos Nieto Navarrete.
Además, señaló, este premio reconoce su constancia y también nos recuerda a todas las personas que cuidan nuestras áreas naturales protegidas: Richar, Teófilo y cada una de las personas premiadas hoy. Cada uno, desde su lugar, nos muestra que proteger la naturaleza requiere compromiso, conocimiento y cercanía con la gente.
Guardaparque destacado
El reconocimiento Guardaparque destacado fue para Richar Antonio Demetrio, guardaparque indígena de la
reserva comunal Asháninka desde 2015. A sus labores de control, vigilancia y prevención de incendios forestales suma la investigación.
Ha participado en el monitoreo de más de 300 colonias de abejas nativas sin aguijón en aproximadamente 40,000 hectáreas de bosque. También ha acompañado a más de 20 jóvenes indígenas en actividades de conservación, uniendo conocimiento científico y saberes de su pueblo.
Artífice de la conservación
Teófilo Torres Tuesta, jefe del
parque nacional Yaguas, recibió el premio Artífice de la conservación. Nacido en una comunidad del río Putumayo y perteneciente al pueblo murui, ha dedicado más de 25 años a la conservación amazónica. Contribuyó a la consolidación de áreas naturales protegidas como los parques nacionales Güeppí-Sekime y Yaguas y las reservas comunales Airo Pai y Huimeki.
Su trabajo con las comunidades ha impulsado la vigilancia participativa y alternativas sostenibles, entre ellas el manejo de taricayas y el aprovechamiento del palo rosa.
La ceremonia también reconoció como Jóvenes conservacionistas destacadas a K’erenda Homet Zambrano Herrera y Ruthmery Pillco Huarcaya.
Personalidad Ambiental
De manera póstuma, Fernando "Pino" Rubio del Valle recibió la distinción Personalidad ambiental. Aliado del Sernanp y referente de la conservación en el Perú, contribuyó a la gestión inicial del
parque nacional Cordillera Azul, donde fortaleció la vigilancia y el patrullaje.
Quienes trabajaron con él recuerdan también su generosidad para compartir conocimientos y formar a nuevas generaciones comprometidas con la protección de los bosques.
El Ministerio del Ambiente, a través del Sernanp, destacó que detrás de estos reconocimientos hay años de trabajo en campo: patrullajes frente a la minería ilegal, vigilancia con las comunidades y formación de quienes hoy continúan conservando las áreas naturales protegidas del Perú. Sus trayectorias muestran que la conservación se sostiene en el esfuerzo diario de quienes conocen el territorio y dedican su vida a cuidarlo.
Sobre el premio
El premio Carlos Ponce del Prado —en homenaje a su trayectoria y compromiso con la conservación— reconoce a quienes dedican su trabajo a conservar la naturaleza del Perú y busca inspirar a nuevas generaciones a seguir ese camino.
Es impulsado por Conservación Internacional, Profonanpe, Andes Amazon Fund, el Ministerio del Ambiente, el Sernanp, la Sociedad Peruana de Derecho Ambiental (SPDA) y la Asociación para la Conservación de la Cuenca Amazónica (ACCA).

title: AIP/ La réhabilitation de l’axe Korhogo-Boundiali améliore la mobilité dans le Nord ivoirien
content:
Abidjan, 22 sept 2026 (AIP) – La réhabilitation de l’axe Korhogo-Boundiali, long de 99 kilomètres, a permis d’améliorer les conditions de circulation des usagers et de renforcer la desserte des localités du Nord ivoirien, a indiqué le Gouvernement dans une publication diffusée lundi 21 septembre 2026 sur les réseaux sociaux.
Cette liaison, qui avait été fortement affectée par la dégradation de la chaussée, offre désormais de meilleures conditions de déplacement aux conducteurs et aux populations qui l’empruntent quotidiennement.
« Avant, c’était compliqué. Je pouvais faire un jour de travail et passer deux jours au garage », témoigne Traoré Losseni, conducteur, évoquant les difficultés liées aux nombreux nids-de-poule qui perturbaient son activité.
Adama Coulibaly, également conducteur, relève pour sa part la facilité des déplacements vers Boundiali et les villages environnants depuis l’amélioration de l’état de la route.
Au-delà de l’amélioration du confort des usagers, la réhabilitation de cet axe contribue à faciliter la circulation des personnes et des marchandises et à renforcer les échanges entre les différentes localités desservies.
Selon le bilan du Gouvernement consacré aux infrastructures routières, plus de 4 000 milliards de FCFA ont été investis dans le secteur routier entre 2011 et 2024.
Sur cette période, 1 927 kilomètres de routes neuves ont été construits et 1 967 kilomètres de routes dégradées ont été renforcées. Le réseau des routes bitumées est, quant à lui, passé de 6 514 à 8 500 kilomètres.
Ces investissements s’inscrivent dans la politique de renforcement des infrastructures routières et d’amélioration de la mobilité sur l’ensemble du territoire national.

title: Varenicline and combination nicotine replacement therapy deemed preferred treatments for tobacco use
content:
A new clinical practice guideline from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and Department of Defense (DoD) provides recommendations for tobacco use treatment. Tobacco and nicotine use among veterans and military service members causes physical and mental health effects and reduces force readiness.
The guideline, published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, recommends varenicline or combination nicotine replacement therapy for cessation and emphasizes the safety and efficacy of pharmacotherapy for patients with mental health conditions. An editorial and a synopsis are also published in the same journal issue.
VA and DoD convened a multidisciplinary panel to review research published between 2014 and 2024 and develop an updated clinical practice guideline for tobacco use treatment. The resulting guideline includes 32 recommendations covering smoking cessation medications, counseling approaches and treatment strategies for adults who use a variety of tobacco and nicotine products.
Key recommendations include motivational interviewing to increase engagement in treatment; using varenicline or combination nicotine replacement therapy to increase abstinence; immediate retreatment for individuals who relapse; and offering treatment even to adults who are not yet ready to quit. The guideline concludes that evidence-based medications and counseling remain the most effective tools for tobacco and nicotine cessation.

title: La fórmula de la longevidad de Herbolario Navarro para sobrevivir 250 años
content:
- La artesanía en extinción de los mantones de Manila de Cindy Crawford o la Casa Real
- Cómo el fundador de Technogym levantó un emporio con 500 euros
Criado tras el mostrador del negocio familiar, como Manolito el amigo de Mafalda, el tercer Pepe Navarro de esta historia regenta una red de 90 ecotiendas propias de alimentación, cosmética y productos para mascotas que cada vez da más frutos.
De pequeńo comercio de barrio a cadena de 90 ecotiendas propias. Fundado por la familia Ribelles en 1771, "era un negocio tradicional de plantas medicinales y hierbas aromáticas. En esa época, la gente acudía a un herbolario cuando tenía algún problema de salud, porque la farmacia no existía como hoy en día ni la medicina estaba tan extendida", recuerda Pepe Navarro (Valencia, 1975), CEO de Herbolario Navarro, que hunde sus raíces en aquel establecimiento muy cerca de la Catedral de Valencia y que en 1926 compró su bisabuela "para que su hijo, mi abuelo, tuviera un medio de vida".
En manos desde hace dos décadas del tercer José Navarro de esta historia y de su madre, Lola Catalá, este proyecto familiar da cada vez más frutos: si cuando heredó la jefatura en 2005 la empresa facturaba 4 millones de euros con "el mayor supermercado ecológico de Espańa, que medía 1.500 metros cuadrados", ahora ronda los 84, con un ebitda superior a los 3,34 millones gracias a su red de tiendas dedicadas a la alimentación, suplementación, cosmética e higiene, puericultura, limpieza y productos para mascotas. La próxima apertura, Córdoba en octubre.
Con todo el negocio bajo su control -tras recomprar las franquicias que un día constituyeron, porque no conseguían "que dieran un servicio de calidad"-, su "vocación es pasarlo a los siguientes", resume el directivo, licenciado en Administración y Dirección de Empresas.
- Es el mediano de tres hermanos. żCómo demuestra que es el sucesor óptimo para liderar el legado?
- Quizá con resultados. Aunque es difícil, eh. Entre que el negocio vaya bien o mediocre, tampoco hay tanta diferencia. Es complicado pasarlo de generación en generación y para garantizar su supervivencia hay que ponerse la gorra de ejecutivo, por decirlo de alguna forma. Debe prevalecer la compańía frente al apellido; si la empresa va bien, la familia va bien.
- żDe tal palo tal astilla? żVe con ganas a los próximos Navarro?
- Aún son muy jóvenes: Nicolás tiene 20 ańos y estudia Administración y Dirección de Empresas; Andrés, 14. Les gusta el negocio, sobre todo porque estamos acostumbrados a cuidarnos y a mantener una buena alimentación. Y conocen las tiendas, porque viajamos juntos con frecuencia a visitarlas. No sé si se dedicarán a esto, no quiero preguntárselo aún. Prefiero dejarles tranquilos, que estudien y que más tarde decidan con total libertad.
- żUsted la tuvo?
- Sí, nunca recibí presiones para hacerme cargo de la empresa, pero era mi día a día: desayunábamos en la tienda, comíamos en la tienda y cenábamos en la tienda. Siempre digo que tenía complejo de Manolito el de Mafalda; los tres hermanos nos hemos criado detrás del mostrador.
- Aunque ahora regente habitualmente un despacho, żmantiene el alma de vendedor?
- Claro. Todos los veranos los pasaba atendiendo y mi despacho actual está dentro de una tienda. No quiero que perdamos el ADN de pequeńa empresa, ni de tendero, que es lo que somos. No podemos olvidar esa vocación de servicio. Tampoco la honestidad, uno de los valores que nos ha hecho llegar hasta aquí.
- żNo todo vale para engordar la cuenta de resultados?
- No estamos aquí para vender el máximo número de productos posible, sino para ayudar a la gente a que tenga buena salud, que es lo importante. Intentamos animar a las personas a que se cuiden.
- Cuando fallece su padre en 2005 y toma las riendas, el negocio era mucho menor que hoy en día. żMantiene su esencia?
- Sí, sigue igual. Esta es una empresa familiar, ahora más grande, en la que, como CEO, ya no puedo estar en contacto directo con los casi 700 empleados. El encargado de tienda es el responsable de trasladar al personal este espíritu de familia y de buen ambiente que buscamos. Aunque es difícil si creces mucho, tratamos de que continúe así.
- żQué cree que opinaría su padre?
- Pienso que le encantaría porque era una persona muy emprendedora y muy innovadora. Creo que estaría muy orgulloso de que vayamos replicando el legado familiar.
- żCuál es la fórmula de la longevidad de esta compańía?
- Yo diría que transmitir de generación en generación el amor y la pasión por este proyecto. Como intentamos ayudar constantemente a que la gente lleve una alimentación adecuada y mantenga una buena salud, cuando el cliente regresa y te dice lo bien que le ha ido lo que le recomendamos, nos motiva a seguir. Ańado también las ganas constantes por mejorar, que no porque siempre se hayan hecho las cosas de determinada manera hay que mantenerlas; hay que adaptarse a los cambios, siendo ágiles, e innovar y sacar a la venta productos nuevos [sus marcas propias suponen el 50% de las ventas].
- żNos cuidamos más ahora?
- Mucho más que nuestros padres. La gente practica más deporte, mira las etiquetas, es más consciente de lo que come. Como se le atribuye a Hipócrates, padre de la Medicina: "Que tu alimento sea tu medicina y tu medicina sea tu alimento". Cuidarse es una tendencia clarísima con mucho recorrido.
- żY cómo se protege la salud de este proyecto familiar?
- Siendo muy consciente, muy humilde y aprendiendo de los grandes. También, siendo atrevido con el crecimiento, pero sensato para no cometer más riesgos de los necesarios; y responsable, que debo defender este legado y casi 700 nóminas; y teniendo visión a largo plazo. Además, es importante profesionalizar la empresa. Soy el único de la familia en un puesto directivo. No me he planteado si dejaría mi cargo en unos ańos, pero creo que sí. Cuando no me vea capaz, aunque me encantan los fregaos y soy muy emprendedor, sí que contrataría a otro CEO.
- żSe duerme bien siendo el jefe y dueńo o necesita remedios (naturales, entiendo) para conciliar el sueńo?
- No todos los días, que muchos me llevo los problemas a casa, pero normalmente sí que lo hago. Y, si no, tengo la solución a mano. Por ejemplo, una infusión relajante.

title: Justice : les greffiers donnent une chance au dialogue
content:
Le Syndicat national du personnel des greffes (SYNAPGREF) suspend son mouvement de grève pour une durée d’un mois. La décision a été prise ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026, lors d’une assemblée générale tenue à N’Djamena.
À l’issue de cette rencontre, le chargé de communication du syndicat, Me Richard Maxhon Baba, a indiqué que cette suspension vise à donner une chance au dialogue engagé avec le ministère de la Justice.
Il rappelle que, lors d’une rencontre tenue le 17 septembre avec la ministre de la Justice, Ndolenodji Alixe Naimbaye, et son équipe, les différentes revendications du syndicat ont été examinées. Le ministère se serait engagé à œuvrer pour leur prise en compte, notamment à travers une relecture des textes concernés.
Lire aussi : Grève sèche des greffiers : un mot d’ordre partiellement suivi
« Compte tenu de la promesse de la ministre, qui s’est engagée à porter haut nos doléances et à ce qu’une solution soit trouvée, nous avons décidé de suspendre et non de lever la grève. Nous sommes un syndicat sérieux », a déclaré Me Richard Maxhon Baba.
La suspension de la grève court jusqu’au 23 octobre 2026. Le syndicat annonce la tenue d’une nouvelle assemblée générale le 26 octobre prochain pour évaluer les avancées obtenues et décider de la suite à donner au mouvement.
Lire aussi : Tchad : après un préavis sans résultat, les greffiers entament une grève sèche d’une semaine
Il faut rappeler que, le SYNAPGREF avait entamé une grève le 17 septembre 2026 pour exiger l’amélioration de ses conditions de travail et la revalorisation de son statut. Après une semaine de paralysie des juridictions, le mouvement est donc suspendu à l’issue de l’assemblée générale de ce 24 septembre.

title: Mike Hammer Engages with Families Receiving Humanitarian Aid in Villa Clara
content:
Mike Hammer, the chief of mission at the U.S. Embassy in Cuba, visited the municipality of Corralillo in Villa Clara this past weekend, particularly the town of Quintín Banderas. His visit aimed to connect with families who benefited from U.S. humanitarian aid packages and ensure the assistance reached those in dire need.
The Embassy captured Hammer's visit in a video shared on its X account, under the hashtag #ConCubanosDeAPie. The footage shows Hammer engaging in conversations with the aid recipients inside their homes.
The visuals highlighted the precarious conditions these families face daily. One woman expressed her gratitude to Hammer upon receiving the aid, saying, "I cried so much. The need is overwhelming," and mentioned that before receiving the package, she had nothing left to eat. Another recipient shared her experience trying the sardines included in the food module.
"Being close to Cubans and listening to them is fundamental to our work," the Embassy noted when posting the video, appreciating the families for "opening their homes and welcoming us warmly."
Follow-Up on Aid Distribution in Villa Clara
This visit was a direct follow-up to the distribution that began in Villa Clara on September 10, when 700 food kits and 700 hygiene kits arrived at Abel Santamaría Airport, targeted for families in Quemado de Güines and Rancho Veloz.
Hammer had previously toured the province from September 12 to 14, visiting vulnerable households in Quemado de Güines and the Cotorra neighborhood. He also met with Bishop Arturo González Amador, the director of Cáritas Santa Clara, and dissident Guillermo "Coco" Fariñas, who had been detained on August 31.
Challenges and Future Aid Plans
During that visit, the Cuban regime launched a disinformation campaign against Hammer in Villa Clara, falsely claiming the food was contaminated—a claim publicly refuted by Cáritas.
The aid Hammer oversees is part of a $100 million program announced by the Trump administration for Cuba. Of this, $60 million is directed through the Catholic Church via Cáritas Cuba and Catholic Relief Services, while $40 million is channeled through other independent organizations, bypassing the Cuban state.
On September 16, the Embassy revealed plans to extend aid to five additional provinces: Camagüey, Ciego de Ávila, Cienfuegos, Matanzas, and Pinar del Río. Shortly thereafter, Cáritas Cienfuegos distributed nearly 700 kits in the Lajas municipality.
Scope and Limitations of the Aid Program
The program is expected to benefit between 100,000 and 120,000 families across Cuba, prioritizing elderly individuals living alone, people with disabilities, pregnant or nursing women, and families with children under five.
Bishop González Amador has cautioned, however, that the assistance has clear limitations: "We can only help the most urgent and distressing cases," stressing that "this is not a permanent social assistance project."
Frequently Asked Questions About U.S. Humanitarian Aid in Cuba
What is the goal of Mike Hammer's visit to Villa Clara?
Mike Hammer's visit aimed to ensure that U.S. humanitarian aid reached those in need and to engage with the families who benefited from the aid packages.
How was the aid distributed across Cuba?
The aid is part of a $100 million program, with $60 million distributed through the Catholic Church and $40 million through other independent organizations, prioritizing vulnerable groups throughout the island.
What challenges have been faced during the aid distribution?
The Cuban regime attempted a disinformation campaign claiming the food was contaminated, which was publicly refuted by Cáritas.

title: Two Emojis of Difference: What Multilingual Affective Generation Benchmarks Actually Measure
content: We audit a multilingual affective generation benchmark eight instruction-tuned LLMs producing emoji summaries for 17,100 Bangla, English and Hindi sentences, with 6,960 human judgements and find its headline conclusions to be artefacts of the measurement instrument rather than properties of the systems. Treating annotators as a random rather than a fixed factor, no system differs significantly from any other ($F(7,14)=0.59$, $p=0.76$), although the conventional analysis declares 19 of 28 pairwise differences significant. Annotator identity explains far more rating variance than system identity, and the winning system changes whenever any single annotator is removed. The ordering that does emerge tracks output length: mean emoji count explains 78.7\% of between-system variance, and a within-item length-matched comparison over 2,599 pairs reverses the leaderboard. We further show that cross-provider anisotropy differences vanish under mean-centring, that per-language token costs change sign with the normalising unit, and that multi-view row-wise splits inflate macro-F1 by $3.1$ points and change the top-ranked system. In place of preference scoring we propose **emoji-affect decodability**, a reference-based probe whose rankings are stable to $\pm0.003$ macro-F1 across seeds.

title: Il viaggio dimenticato delle sedonere: le donne della Valcellina che sfidarono le montagne con un carretto raccontate in un docufilm
content:
Il viaggio dimenticato delle sedonere: le donne della Valcellina che sfidarono le montagne con un carretto raccontate in un docufilm
C’è un’immagine che sembra arrivare da un altro tempo: donne coi fazzoletti a riparare la testa, carretti tirati da mani nude, la strada davanti e chilometri da percorrere. Dietro, alle loro spalle, una valle, una casa, una famiglia e, davanti, un mondo del tutto sconosciuto. Erano le sedonere, le donne delle montagne friulane che tra la fine dell’Ottocento e la prima metà del Novecento hanno lasciato i paesi dell’alta Valcellina, ai confini con il Vajont, per scendere verso la pianura e le città del Nord Italia. A cercare fortuna.
A raccogliere questa fragile memoria è FORA PAL MONT – I passi rimasti (Fora pal mont è letteralmente “fuori per il mondo, in giro per il mondo”, ndr), l’ultimo documentario diretto da Lorena Trevisan e Michele Pastrello, che incontra sei delle donne che hanno vissuto quella stagione e che oggi, tra i novanta e i cento anni, raccontano in prima persona il viaggio delle sedonere. Le loro voci riportano alla luce un pezzo di storia rimasto a lungo ai margini: quello di donne che, partendo dalla montagna, hanno attraversato l’Italia e conquistato spazi di autonomia in un’epoca in cui il loro ruolo era ancora fortemente limitato.
Con sé avevano decine di manufatti e oggetti di legno, soprattutto i sedon (i mestoli e gli utensili da cucina, da cui deriva il loro nome), e li vendevano lungo il cammino. Partivano per settimane, a volte per mesi, e dormivano dove capitava: nei fienili, nelle stalle, presso le famiglie che offrivano loro un posto per la notte. Nessun viaggio romantico, quindi, ma fatica allo stato puro mista a freddo e solitudine e partenze che nascevano dalla necessità. Le comunità di montagna erano povere, isolate, con poche possibilità di lavoro e così, il denaro guadagnato dalle sedonere serviva a sostenere l’economia familiare e a portare qualcosa in più nelle case.
Eppure, quei viaggi produssero un effetto inatteso. Per molte donne, infatti, raccontano Pastrello e Trevisan, rappresentarono il primo spazio di autonomia fuori dai confini del paese natale. Lontane dalle vicissitudini di una comunità, imparavano strade nuove, incontravano persone diverse, gestivano denaro, prendevano decisioni. In un’epoca in cui il ruolo femminile era spesso confinato alla famiglia e alla casa, una sedonera era una donna che camminava da sola nel mondo. Una lavoratrice, una commerciante, una figura che oggi potremmo definire indipendente, ma che allora veniva semplicemente considerata una necessità della vita.
Hanno fatto tanto per se stesse e per la valle – spiega Lorena Trevisan -, inconsapevoli di essere state piccola parte attiva di un processo di cambiamento culturale. Ed è proprio per questo che le loro testimonianze sono ancora così contemporanee, soprattutto per noi donne. Ci ricordano che l’emancipazione non è qualcosa che è cominciato un giorno grazie a una singola persona, ma è un percorso costruito da molte persone e da più ceti sociali, fatto di tante piccole libertà conquistate, spesso senza nemmeno chiamarle così. Ed è un percorso ancora in divenire. Le loro storie partivano dalla valle, tanto tempo fa, ma in un certo senso arrivano ancora fino a noi.
Una storia rimasta ai margini
Come tante storie di donne del Novecento, anche quella delle sedonere è rimasta per lungo tempo ai margini della memoria collettiva. La sociologa Casimira Grandi ha usato l’espressione “presenza assente” per descrivere proprio questa condizione: donne fondamentali nella vita economica e sociale delle comunità, ma spesso poco presenti nei racconti ufficiali, negli archivi e nella narrazione storica.
Le sedonere c’erano. Hanno lavorato e contribuito alla sopravvivenza delle loro famiglie e dei loro paesi, ma il loro viaggio è rimasto quasi invisibile.
Le donne lavoravano nei campi, con gli animali, in casa e in molte attività integrative – racconta Pastrello -,pur con diritti fortemente limitati tanto è vero che fino al 1919 vigeva l’autorizzazione maritale. La Prima guerra mondiale, per forza di cose, rese più visibile il loro ruolo economico, ma il fascismo ricondusse presto la donna al modello ideologico di moglie e madre, limitandone ambizioni, formazione e carriera. Ancora nel 1931 una larghissima percentuale di donne veniva classificata nelle statistiche con il fumoso “attendenti a casa”. È in questa contraddizione che si inserisce la storia delle sedonere di Fora Pal Mont. Erano donne ambulanti che svolgevano un mestiere percepito come maschile, viaggiavano tantissimo chi trainando un carretto ed altre con ingombranti cassettiere, dormivano sotto le stelle. Si sentivano commercianti, anche se difficilmente potevano rivendicare apertamente quel ruolo. Nel Nord Italia esistono pochissimi casi analoghi di lavoro ambulante femminile organizzato su questa scala.
Il documentario che restituisce voce alle ultime sedonere
Il docufilm – sulle note di Fémene (del cantautore Franco Giordani su poesia della poetessa Bianca Borsatti) – incontra sei delle ultime sedonere – Teresa, Luigia, Vittorina, Fiorina, Luciana, Carolina (la più giovane ha 91 anni, Luigia ne ha 102) – che attraverso i loro racconti riportano alla luce quel mondo fatto di fatica, coraggio, ironia e resistenza. Sono storie di donne che hanno attraversato un’Italia diversa: quella delle valli isolate, delle famiglie numerose, del lavoro manuale e delle partenze senza sapere sempre cosa avrebbe aspettato loro dall’altra parte della montagna. Nei loro racconti c’è la durezza del viaggio, ma anche il ricordo di una libertà conquistata passo dopo passo.
La storia delle sedonere appartiene a un territorio preciso, l’alta Valcellina, ma vuole parlare di tutte quelle donne che hanno lavorato senza essere chiamate “lavoratrici”, che hanno sostenuto economie familiari senza comparire nei libri, che hanno modificato lentamente le proprie comunità senza entrare nei racconti ufficiali.
Ed è questa la domanda che il documentario ci lascia: quante storie di donne abbiamo perso perché nessuno si è fermato ad ascoltarle?
FORA PAL MONT – I passi rimasti ha iniziato nel 2026 il suo percorso nei festival e nelle rassegne italiane: è stato selezionato da Le Giornate della Luce presso Cinemazero di Pordenone, Nuovi Mondi Film Festival, Edera Film Festival di Treviso come evento speciale, Mario Puzo Film Festival ed ETNOfilmFest di Este. Ha inoltre ricevuto la Menzione d’Onore della Giuria al Premio Vittorio De Seta 2026.

title: TRPV1 Activation via a Three‐Stage Adaptive Heat‐Absorbing Hydrogel Drives Neurovascular–Immune Coupling
content: A three‐stage adaptive heat‐absorbing hydrogel converts near‐infrared light into precisely regulated thermal and biochemical signals for on‐demand TRPV1 activation. By integrating sprayable conformal delivery, controlled photothermal modulation, and synchronized biochemical stimulation, the platform restores neurovascular–immune coupling and accelerates diabetic wound healing, offering a programmable strategy for channel‐targeted regenerative therapy. ABSTRACT Impaired neurovascular–immune coupling severely hampers chronic wound healing. Although the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channel represents a promising therapeutic target, its therapeutic application remains limited by imprecise activation. Here, we developed a three‐stage adaptive and heat‐absorbing hydrogel (termed HMCG) that enables programmable and localized TRPV1 activation under near‐infrared (NIR) irradiation. HMCG forms reversible boronate ester bonds between PVA and TSPBA, enabling a sol–aerosol–gel adaptive with sprayable handling, self‐adaptation, and conformal coverage of complex wound topologies. This dynamic behavior ensures close biointerface contact and controlled thermal regulation during stimulation. Embedded Ca‐gallic acid metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) act as photon‐thermal converters, where ligand‐metal charge transfer and π–π stacking drive rapid nonradiative relaxation, leading to efficient and controllable heat absorption. Brief NIR exposure triggers the sustained release of capsaicin and Ca2+, elevating the local temperature to 43°C, within the TRPV1 activation window and with a reduced risk of nonspecific thermal overstimulation. Together, the tri‐stage adaptive design helps buffer heat, maintains topological adaptability, and synchronizes mild photothermal and biochemical cues. This controlled light‐heat‐chemical coupling supports the restoration of neurovascular–immune coupling and promotes tissue regeneration in diabetic skin lesion models, establishing a controlled, programmable platform for TRPV1‐targeted regenerative therapy.
